quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Morning Routine] Every morning at seven, Kofi makes his bed, feeds his cat, and sits down to breakfast.
quests.question: What do Kofi's morning habits suggest?
options: He has to hurry to get to work on time.
They follow the same pattern each day.
He prefers cooking to any other activity.
He lives alone with his cat.
quests.correctAnswer: They follow the same pattern each day.
quests.hint: Notice the word "every" and the order of his tasks.
quests.explanation: Kofi does the same tasks, in the same order, at the same time each morning. That repeated pattern tells us his mornings follow a routine, even though the word "routine" never appears.
clueWords: makes his bed, feeds his cat

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Arrivals Hall] Hana runs across the arrivals hall and hugs her grandmother tightly. "Two whole years!" she says.
quests.question: What does Hana's reaction suggest about her and her grandmother?
options: They argued the last time they met.
They see each other most weekends.
They met for the first time today.
They have been apart for a long time.
quests.correctAnswer: They have been apart for a long time.
quests.hint: Think about what "two whole years" tells you about the last time they saw each other.
quests.explanation: Hana runs to hug her grandmother and mentions two whole years. Her excitement and the length of time show that this is a reunion after a long separation.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Before the Exam] Before the exam, Tomás reads his notes once more, checks that his pens work, and arrives twenty minutes early.
quests.question: Why is Tomás doing all of these things?
options: He wants to feel ready and avoid last-minute problems.
The teacher asked him to help set up the room.
He is worried that this year's exam questions will be very different from last year's.
He is unsure which day the exam is on.
quests.correctAnswer: He wants to feel ready and avoid last-minute problems.
quests.hint: Ask what each small action would protect him from.
quests.explanation: Rereading notes, testing pens, and arriving early are all ways of preventing trouble. Together they show that Tomás wants to be prepared.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Puddles] Nina shakes her umbrella by the door. Her socks are soaked from stepping in puddles on the way home.
quests.question: What was the weather probably like outside?
options: Strong winds had been blowing all day.
It had been raining.
The sun had been very strong.
There had been a heavy frost.
quests.correctAnswer: It had been raining.
quests.hint: What creates puddles, and why would someone carry an umbrella?
quests.explanation: An umbrella and puddles both point to rain. Together they make rain far more likely than strong sun, wind, or frost.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Saturday Queue] The line at Rosa's Bakery reaches the corner every Saturday. Some customers say they would wait an hour if they had to.
quests.question: What does the queue suggest about Rosa's Bakery?
options: Many people think its food is worth waiting for.
It does not have enough workers to serve people.
It is cheaper than every other bakery in town.
It has just opened for the first time.
quests.correctAnswer: Many people think its food is worth waiting for.
quests.hint: Why would people stand in a long line on purpose?
quests.explanation: People who queue every week and are willing to wait an hour must feel the bakery is worth it. The passage says nothing about price, opening date, or staff, so those ideas are unsupported.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Just Missed It] Deepak reaches the bus stop as the bus pulls away. He looks at his watch, sighs, and starts to walk.
quests.question: How does Deepak most likely feel?
options: Curious about the driver's route.
Annoyed that he missed the bus.
Pleased to have a chance to walk.
Relieved that the bus was crowded.
quests.correctAnswer: Annoyed that he missed the bus.
quests.hint: Look at what he does right after watching the bus leave.
quests.explanation: Checking his watch and sighing show irritation. He is walking because the bus left, not because he wanted the exercise.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [On Repeat] Yuki plays the same album on the bus, in the kitchen, and while she does homework. Her brother says he can sing every song by now.
quests.question: What does Yuki's listening habit suggest about the album?
options: She likes it a lot.
Her brother bought it as a gift for her.
She has only just found out about it.
She is practising it for a school concert.
quests.correctAnswer: She likes it a lot.
quests.hint: How often does she choose it, and where?
quests.explanation: Playing one album in so many places shows that she really enjoys it. Her brother knowing every song also suggests it has been playing for a while. Nothing points to a concert or a gift.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Second Helping] Bruno finishes his rice and chicken, then asks for more chicken. The vegetables sit untouched on the edge of his plate.
quests.question: What does Bruno's behaviour suggest?
options: He was told the vegetables were undercooked and is avoiding them for that reason.
He likes the chicken better than the vegetables.
He dislikes all of the food.
He has never tasted chicken before.
quests.correctAnswer: He likes the chicken better than the vegetables.
quests.hint: Compare what he asks for with what he leaves.
quests.explanation: He asks for more chicken but ignores the vegetables. That contrast shows a preference. If he were full, or disliked everything, he would not ask for more.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Window Shopping] Ivana looks at the blue bag in the shop window, then at her purse, then back at the window. Finally she goes in and asks the price.
quests.question: What does Ivana's behaviour suggest?
options: She is seriously thinking about buying the bag.
She is waiting for a friend to arrive.
She is looking for a gift for a friend who has a birthday soon.
She works in the shop.
quests.correctAnswer: She is seriously thinking about buying the bag.
quests.hint: Follow the order of her looks and what she finally does.
quests.explanation: She compares the bag with her purse, then asks the price. These steps show she is considering a purchase, not just admiring a display.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Whistle] A whistle blows. Players in red and white run up and down the wet grass while people shout from the side.
quests.question: Where is this scene most likely taking place?
options: At an outdoor market.
At an outdoor sports game.
At a gym class held indoors.
At a school assembly.
quests.correctAnswer: At an outdoor sports game.
quests.hint: Combine the sound, the clothes, and the place where people are running.
quests.explanation: A whistle, team colours, running on grass, and shouting spectators fit a sports game. Each clue alone could suit other places, but together they do not.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Before Sunrise] Ali switches on his bedside lamp, rubs his eyes, and looks at the dark window. A moment later his alarm rings.
quests.question: At what point in the day does this scene most likely take place?
options: Around lunchtime.
Late in the afternoon.
Very early in the morning.
Just after dinner.
quests.correctAnswer: Very early in the morning.
quests.hint: Why would he need a lamp, and what is his alarm for?
quests.explanation: He rubs his eyes, needs a lamp, and the window is dark, and his alarm is about to ring. This fits waking up before dawn better than any other time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Not Again] Smoke drifts from the oven, and Tessa opens the window wide. "Not again," she mutters, waving a towel at the air.
quests.question: What most likely caused the smoke?
options: She burned the food she was cooking.
The oven was just installed today.
She is testing the smoke alarm on purpose.
A neighbour lit a bonfire outside.
quests.correctAnswer: She burned the food she was cooking.
quests.hint: What does "Not again" tell you about how often this happens?
quests.explanation: Smoke from the oven, an open window, and "Not again" suggest she has burned food before and has just done it once more.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Handing Back Tests] The teacher hands back the tests. Jae-won looks at his paper, smiles, and quickly shows it to the girl beside him.
quests.question: How does Jae-won most likely feel about his result?
options: Confused by the teacher's comments.
Bored by the whole lesson.
Pleased, and a little proud.
Worried about what his parents will say.
quests.correctAnswer: Pleased, and a little proud.
quests.hint: Notice his face and what he wants to do with the paper.
quests.explanation: Smiling and showing the paper to a classmate are things people do when they are happy with a result and want to share it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Halfway Through the Film] Halfway through the film, Ines pulls her sweater over her knees, grips a cushion, and peeks out between her fingers.
quests.question: How is Ines probably feeling?
options: Sleepy after a long day.
Cold, and wishing the heating were higher.
Bored with the story.
Frightened by what she is watching.
quests.correctAnswer: Frightened by what she is watching.
quests.hint: One clue could mean cold. Check whether the other two clues fit it.
quests.explanation: The sweater alone might suggest cold, but gripping a cushion and peeking through her fingers are things people do when scared. All three clues together point to fear.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Second Hour] Mr. Adeyemi glances at the clock, taps his pen on the table, and sighs as the meeting enters its second hour.
quests.question: What does Mr. Adeyemi's behaviour suggest?
options: He is eager for the meeting to continue.
He is confused about the topic being discussed.
He is losing patience with the meeting.
He is taking careful notes for a report.
quests.correctAnswer: He is losing patience with the meeting.
quests.hint: What do glancing at the clock and tapping a pen usually show?
quests.explanation: Checking the time, tapping, and sighing all show restlessness. Together they suggest he wants the meeting to end soon.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Back at Two] The café door has a handwritten sign: "Back at 2:00." At 1:45 the owner is sitting on a bench outside, finishing a sandwich.
quests.question: Why is the café closed?
options: The owner has stepped out for a lunch break.
The owner is at a meeting with the bank about the café's rent.
The café has closed down for good.
The owner is waiting for a delivery.
quests.correctAnswer: The owner has stepped out for a lunch break.
quests.hint: Put the sign together with what the owner is doing.
quests.explanation: "Back at 2:00" tells us the closure is temporary, and the owner eating a sandwich nearby explains why. Nothing suggests the café is closing permanently.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Silent Room] The classroom is unusually quiet. Every student is looking down at a desk, and the only sound is pencils scratching.
quests.question: What are the students most likely doing?
options: Discussing a topic in small groups.
Watching a video together.
Listening to the teacher tell a story.
Working alone on something written.
quests.correctAnswer: Working alone on something written.
quests.hint: Listen for the only sound mentioned.
quests.explanation: Silence, eyes on the desk, and pencils scratching show that students are writing on their own. Groups and videos would involve talking or sound.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Dark Street] All the lights on Hill Street are off. In his kitchen, Mr. Bose lights two candles and searches a drawer for a torch.
quests.question: What has most likely happened?
options: The power has gone out.
Everyone on the street has gone to sleep.
Mr. Bose is trying to save money on electricity.
The street is having a special candlelit evening.
quests.correctAnswer: The power has gone out.
quests.hint: Why would someone need a torch in his own kitchen?
quests.explanation: If only his lights were off, he could use another room. But the whole street is dark and he needs candles and a torch, which points to a power cut.
clueWords: All the lights on Hill Street
searches a drawer for a torch

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Grey Sky] The sky turns dark, and the wind starts to pick up. Marta looks at the washing on the line and hurries outside.
quests.question: What is Marta most likely about to do?
options: Close the windows to keep the house warm.
Hang up some more washing.
Bring the washing in before it gets wet.
Take a photograph of the clouds.
quests.correctAnswer: Bring the washing in before it gets wet.
quests.hint: Connect what she sees in the sky with what she notices on the line.
quests.explanation: Dark sky and rising wind suggest rain may be coming. Marta hurries toward washing that would get wet, so she is probably going to rescue it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Coin Jar] Kwame has been saving coins in a jar for months. Today he counts them carefully, puts them in a bag, and walks to the bike shop.
quests.question: What will Kwame most likely do at the shop?
options: Sell his old bicycle.
Ask the owner for a job.
Return something he bought earlier.
Buy something with his savings.
quests.correctAnswer: Buy something with his savings.
quests.hint: Why would someone save money for months and then carry it to a shop?
quests.explanation: Months of saving, careful counting, and a trip to the shop make the most sense if he is about to pay for something he has wanted.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Guests at Three] The recipe says the cake must cool for an hour before icing. Dalia's guests arrive at three, and it is already 2:20. She sets the tin by the open window and turns on a fan.
quests.question: What is Dalia trying to do?
options: Keep the cake warm until the guests arrive.
Bake a second cake before three.
Hide the cake from her guests.
Cool the cake more quickly.
quests.correctAnswer: Cool the cake more quickly.
quests.hint: Compare how much time she has with how much time the recipe asks for.
quests.explanation: The recipe needs an hour, but she has under forty minutes. The open window and fan show she is trying to speed up the cooling.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Waiting Room] "Please have a seat, Ms. Okafor," says the young man, pulling out a chair. "Mr. Reyes will see you in a few minutes."
quests.question: What is the young man most likely to be?
options: Mr. Reyes's manager.
Ms. Okafor's son.
Someone who works in the office.
Another visitor waiting to be seen.
quests.correctAnswer: Someone who works in the office.
quests.hint: Notice who he speaks for and who he speaks to.
quests.explanation: He offers a seat and announces when Mr. Reyes will be ready, as if he manages the visit. That is what an office assistant or receptionist does.
clueWords: will see you in a few minutes

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Little Brother] Leila's little brother follows her everywhere. He copies her handwriting and wears her old school scarf, even on warm days.
quests.question: How does the little brother most likely feel about Leila?
options: He is trying to annoy her.
He looks up to her.
He is jealous of her friends.
He wants her to leave home.
quests.correctAnswer: He looks up to her.
quests.hint: What do copying and wearing someone's things usually show?
quests.explanation: Following, imitating, and wearing her scarf even in warm weather show that he admires her and wants to be like her.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Runaway Dog] Whenever the neighbours' dog gets out, Mrs. Kim is the first one running after it. Yesterday she brought it back with a bowl of water and a big smile.
quests.question: What does Mrs. Kim's behaviour suggest about her attitude to the dog?
options: She dislikes her neighbours.
She is the dog's owner.
She is fond of the dog.
She is afraid of dogs.
quests.correctAnswer: She is fond of the dog.
quests.hint: Read carefully whose dog it is, then look at how she treats it.
quests.explanation: The dog belongs to the neighbours, so Mrs. Kim is not the owner. Her eagerness to help, the water, and the smile show she cares about it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [After the Film] After the movie, Grace tells her friends, "I'm going again this weekend, and I'm taking my brother."
quests.question: What is Grace's opinion of the movie?
options: She thought it was too long.
She only watched it to be polite.
She thought it was very good.
She was disappointed by the ending.
quests.correctAnswer: She thought it was very good.
quests.hint: Would you pay to see something a second time if you did not enjoy it?
quests.explanation: Planning to see it again, and inviting her brother too, shows that she enjoyed it and wants others to see it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Bare Branches] The trees on Elm Street are bare, and children in thick coats kick through piles of brown leaves.
quests.question: Which time of year is it most likely?
options: Midsummer.
Late autumn.
Late spring.
Early spring.
quests.correctAnswer: Late autumn.
quests.hint: Look at the trees and at what is on the ground.
quests.explanation: Trees that have lost their leaves, leaves piled on the ground, and thick coats point to late autumn. In spring, the trees would be showing buds or new leaves.
clueWords: trees on Elm Street are bare

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Stairs Today] Sofia presses the lift button four times. A sign taped over it says "Please use the stairs today." She sighs, picks up her bag, and starts climbing.
quests.question: Why is Sofia climbing the stairs instead of taking the lift?
options: It has been replaced by an escalator.
It is not available at the moment.
It is only for visitors.
It is quicker than the stairs, so she waited.
quests.correctAnswer: It is not available at the moment.
quests.hint: Why would a sign be taped over the button?
quests.explanation: The taped sign and the word "today" show a temporary problem. Sofia gives up pressing the button and climbs, which confirms the lift is not available.
clueWords: presses the lift button four times

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Early Again] Ayaan returns his library books a day early and writes his name neatly on every form he fills in.
quests.question: What kind of person is Ayaan most likely to be?
options: Adventurous and impatient.
Forgetful and careless.
Generous and talkative.
Careful and responsible.
quests.correctAnswer: Careful and responsible.
quests.hint: What do his small habits have in common?
quests.explanation: Returning books early and writing neatly are small habits that show care and responsibility. They do not point to forgetfulness or impatience.
clueWords: returns his library books a day early

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Window Seat] "Would you like the window seat?" the woman asks. "No, no, you take it," says Pedro, gripping the armrest as the plane starts to move.
quests.question: What does Pedro's reaction reveal about how he feels?
options: He plans to sleep for the whole flight.
He is in a hurry to get off the plane.
He is annoyed with the woman.
He feels nervous about flying.
quests.correctAnswer: He feels nervous about flying.
quests.hint: Look at what his hand is doing at that moment.
quests.explanation: Most people would enjoy a window seat, but Pedro refuses it quickly while gripping the armrest as the plane moves. These clues suggest nervousness.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Price Tag] Sara checks the price tag on the jacket, puts it back on the rail, and walks to the sale section.
quests.question: Why did Sara put the jacket back?
options: She dislikes the colour of the jacket.
She thinks the jacket would be too warm and is looking for something lighter.
The jacket costs more than she wants to spend.
The jacket is the wrong size for her.
quests.correctAnswer: The jacket costs more than she wants to spend.
quests.hint: What did she look at right before she put the jacket back?
quests.explanation: She checks the price, puts the jacket back, and goes straight to the sale section. The sequence points to price as her reason.
